issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness goes through rng from the seed. The change only swaps the single best packing for an elite pool of up to 8 distinct packings, and later restarts perturb one picked with 1/rank weights.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. pool[k][1] and pool[k][2] are passed as the tuple (c, r), the same form the incumbent passed as best. Every packing in the pool has already been through _repair, so the returned packing is valid. Dropping a packing whose sum is within 1e-6 of one already in the pool is reasonable.

Small edge case, same as the incumbent: if no restart finishes within TIME_FRACTION*time_limit, pool[0] raises an IndexError. The old code would return None in that case, so this is not a new risk in practice.

The numbers support the call. The candidate (-2.6360, about the best published value, which is plausible) beats the incumbent (-2.6349) by 0.0011. With noise sd 0.0023 for each job and one run on each side, the standard error of the difference is 0.0023*sqrt(2) ≈ 0.00325, so z ≈ 0.34. That matches the harness's 0.350 within rounding of the displayed values. This is not significant, so reject on this evidence is consistent. With n=1 on each side the test has little power: if a replicate fits the budget, it may be worth one, since the change is simple and plausibly helps.
